clue.text: It's rather provocative, as the upper form's demonstrated

definitions.text: It's rather provocative, as the upper form's demonstrated

parts.words: It's rather provocative, as the upper form's demonstrated
parts.note: a daring style of dress, hinted at by a school's top form showing it has gone without its upper garment

explanation.surface: A teacher remarks that the top class has shown some rather provocative behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper form' reads like a senior school class, but it means the top half of the body, shown uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without any upper garment is a deliberately revealing, rather provocative way of appearing.

clue.text: Count needed reprimand

definitions.meaning: to count off one by one, an old sense of tell

explanation.surface: An aristocrat had to give someone a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to number off in turn, and to scold.

clue.text: Military punishment for those named?

parts.note: a punishment drill marching in full kit, punned as exercises for people with the surname Pack

explanation.surface: Asks what army punishment suits certain people.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a military punishment of marching up and down in full kit.

clue.text: Turn out in green suede

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Showing up in green suede.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a result, to turn out.

clue.text: Even now, biography is an art-form

parts.note: still means even now, yet
a life is a written biography

explanation.surface: Even now, biography counts as an art form.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of arranged objects such as fruit is a recognised genre of art.

clue.text: Call to join total battle

indicators.note: one piece joins the next, side by side in a row

parts.note: a total is a sum
Mons was a First World War battle in Belgium

explanation.surface: A summons to join a full-scale battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A summons is an official call to appear somewhere.

clue.text: Seaman at first joins the rest to fix propeller

indicators.note: one piece joins the next, side by side in a row
only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the crew are all the rest of the ship's company

explanation.surface: A sailor is first to join the others fixing the propeller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fix' only links here, though it plays on the other sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's propeller is commonly called its screw.

clue.text: Great frequency with which little girl's seen on a bike

parts.note: Meg is a short girl's name
to bike is to cycle

explanation.surface: A girl's seen out on a bike making a great frequency of trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A megacycle is an old unit of a million cycles per second, a large frequency.

clue.text: Cut, as silk maybe

definitions.meaning: silk treated with oil to make it waterproof

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: slang for drunk, and treated with oil like waterproof silk.

clue.text: Medical man who has no time for fish

indicators.note: the fish goes without the letter, which is removed

parts.note: a sturgeon is a fish

explanation.surface: A doctor with no time to eat fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor who operates.

clue.text: All relevant points covered in maths lesson

definitions.text: All relevant points covered in maths lesson

parts.words: All relevant points covered in maths lesson
parts.note: reads like a teacher covering every key point, but describes the geometric set of all points meeting a condition

explanation.surface: A maths lesson that covers all the relevant points.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this term names the set of all points satisfying a given condition.

clue.text: Such habits unsuitable for a professional soldier

definitions.text: Such habits unsuitable for a professional soldier

parts.words: Such habits unsuitable for a professional soldier
parts.note: habits that are erratic, and also the term for a soldier not in the regular army

explanation.surface: Some habits are not suitable for a career soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The word describes erratic habits and also a fighter outside the regular, professional army.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic habits are unsteady ones, and a non-professional fighter outside the standing army bears the same name.

clue.text: Member of fraternity loosely followed Dominican leader

indicators.note: held loosely, the letters fall out of order and rearrange
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brotherhood member loosely followed the Dominican leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges FOLLOWED plus D, the first letter of 'Dominican'. The Oddfellows are a British friendly society.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oddfellows are a fraternal friendly society, so one of them is a member of that brotherhood.

clue.text: Rotter about to expose group of activists

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, a bounder
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A cad is about to expose a group of activists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to expose' only links the wordplay to the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained political activists.

clue.text: Was cooking chips -one nicked by Alf?

indicators.note: the man's name takes the letter in, as though nicked or cut into it

parts.note: the question mark makes Alf just an example of an ordinary chap's name, so another such name, Fred, will do
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone was frying chips when one was pinched by Alf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alf?' with its question mark stands for any everyday man's name; Fred fits the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips are cooked in hot fat, so cooking them in that way is the verb's past form here.

clue.text: Discourage male cleaner

parts.note: to discourage is to deter
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Try to put off a male cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent.

clue.text: Process of reasoning that can make Labour get a move on

definitions.meaning: reasoning from particular cases to a general rule

definitions.text: that can make Labour get a move on
definitions.meaning: a medical procedure that starts childbirth labour artificially

explanation.surface: A method of reasoning that could speed up the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: reasoning from cases to rules, and artificially starting childbirth.

clue.text: One expected to set off and do a rotten shift

indicators.note: the letters shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A worker expected to set off and do a lousy shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is a device whose job is to set off an explosion.

clue.text: One who sings, doing well — could be a soldier

parts.note: in form means performing well
an ant may be a soldier, the caste that defends the colony

explanation.surface: A singer doing well who could become a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sings' is slang for telling tales to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing is slang for informing on others, so a singer is a police informer.

clue.text: Allowance for a patch

definitions.meaning: a small rented plot of land for growing vegetables

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a share handed out, and a small rented vegetable plot in Britain.

clue.text: I may charge account holder admitting source of currency

indicators.note: the outer pieces let another letter in

parts.note: a user holds and operates something

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bank customer admits where currency comes from and may face charges.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is someone who brings a charge against another.

clue.text: The Spanish ending French being mischievous

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
fin is French for end

explanation.surface: A Spaniard ending up as a mischievous Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are impish, so something elf-like is playfully mischievous.

clue.text: Plant that is given means to adapt

indicators.note: to adapt is to alter, so the letters change order

parts.note: ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A plant is given the means to adapt.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesia is a flowering garden plant from South Africa.

clue.text: Office cleaner carrying unit

indicators.note: the cleaner holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman
unit means one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An office cleaner carrying a unit of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' looks like a workplace but means a post held, as in taking the chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair is the office of presiding over a meeting or committee.

clue.text: Touches bar when jumping across it

indicators.note: one piece leaps across the other, surrounding it

parts.note: as can mean when
bar means except, as does but

explanation.surface: Someone brushes a bar while leaping over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to touch along a border, as adjoining land does.

clue.text: Star appearing in Royal Marine pageant free

indicators.note: set free, the letters break loose into a new order

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A star appearing in a free Royal Marine pageant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges PAGEANT together with RM; 'appearing in' tells you RM joins that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star figure.

clue.text: Work given up to harbour stolen picture

indicators.note: the outer piece shelters the other
in a down clue, given up reads the word upwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
hot is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: Work handed in to hide a stolen picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' turns OP into PO, which holds HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a picture taken by camera.

clue.text: Commodity the French dropped off a lorry

indicators.note: the letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: an article is an item of goods
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Goods the French dropped off a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: An artic is short for an articulated lorry.

clue.text: Brass vessel that's used in dinner service

parts.note: brass is cheek or impudence, as is sauce
a boat is a vessel

explanation.surface: A brass dish that is part of a dinner service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like the metal, but means nerve or cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravy jug of this kind is a standard piece of a dinner set.

clue.text: Toils in bunkers

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: snares or nets, and sand hazards on a golf course.

clue.text: One has to stir minced duck into this dish

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
minced means chopped up, so the letters are cut and remixed

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A cook has to stir minced duck into a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minced' rearranges TO STIR into RISTTO, and 'into' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A risotto is an Italian rice dish, which can indeed include minced duck.

clue.text: Some cheese by kid's bed — maybe maid eats it

indicators.note: the girl takes the other piece inside her

parts.note: a maid is a girl, and Rita is one example of a girl's name
a cot is a child's bed

explanation.surface: Some cheese by a child's bed, which the maid might eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.
